description: We are a team passionate about technology, creativity, and space exploration, aiming to develop an innovative solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary:
Welcome to Polar Base: Lunar Mission! What if you had to lead a team of astronauts and build a sustainable base on the Moon? In this educational strategy simulator, players take command of four astronauts stationed at the lunar south pole for a 30-day mission. Their goal is to keep the crew alive, conduct scientific experiments, and survive the extreme conditions of the lunar environment.
But survival is not easy. Players must manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and energy while facing challenges including the 14-day lunar night, extreme cold, solar storms, radiation, and hazardous lunar dust. Every decision matters: should you invest in solar panels, reserve batteries, or a nuclear reactor? Should you explore for lunar ice or conserve resources?
Inspired by real NASA research and space exploration technologies, the game transforms complex scientific concepts into interactive challenges for young learners, encouraging critical thinking, resource management, and an understanding of the engineering decisions required for future lunar missions.
details:
The Mission

Players must manage a lunar base for 30 days, representing a complete lunar mission cycle. They must achieve three main objectives:

  • Keep all four astronauts alive.
  • Collect at least 100 science points.
  • Survive the lunar night without running out of essential resources.

How Does Our Solution Work?

Players take the role of mission commander and make strategic decisions using limited Action Points (AP). Each action affects the base's resources and determines the success or failure of the mission.

Throughout the game, players must:

  • Manage Life Support: Maintain oxygen, water, and food supplies to keep the astronauts alive.
  • Generate Energy: Balance solar panels, reserve batteries, and a 10 kW fission reactor to maintain power during the lunar night.
  • Explore the Moon: Extract water ice, conduct scientific experiments, and collect research points.
  • Maintain Equipment: Remove lunar dust to protect spacesuits, solar panels, and other equipment.
  • Respond to Emergencies: Make critical decisions during solar storms, extreme cold, and micrometeorite impacts.

Every decision involves a trade-off between resource consumption, scientific progress, and crew survival.

The Benefits

The project aims to:

  • Introduce children to lunar exploration and astronaut mission planning.
  • Explain real scientific challenges associated with living on the Moon.
  • Develop problem-solving, critical thinking, and resource-management skills.
  • Demonstrate how NASA research and space technologies contribute to future lunar missions.
  • Make STEM education more interactive and accessible through gameplay.

Our Goal

Our goal is to transform real lunar exploration challenges into an engaging educational experience where young players learn that establishing a sustainable base on the Moon requires science, teamwork, planning, and responsible resource management.

Tools and Technologies Used

Coding Languages:
HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript were used to develop the game's structure, visual design, interactive elements, gameplay mechanics, resource management systems, and bilingual interface (English and Spanish).

Development Environment:
Visual Studio Code was used as the main code editor for writing, organizing, and debugging the game's files.

Data Sources:
NASA's official scientific resources and educational materials were used as references for lunar exploration, the Moon's south pole, water ice, solar energy, nuclear fission power, life-support systems, lunar dust, radiation, and the environmental challenges of living on the Moon.

Character Design:
The game features four astronaut crew members representing a lunar exploration team. Their design and roles support the educational theme of teamwork, space exploration, and mission management.

Game Assets and Audio:
Visual assets, illustrations, background music, and sound effects are used to create an immersive lunar mission experience.

Version Control and Publishing:
GitHub is used to store, organize, and manage the project's source code and development files.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

AI tools were used as supportive resources throughout the development process:

  • ChatGPT (OpenAI): Assisted in generating, debugging, and improving the game's code, as well as supporting development workflows connected to GitHub.
  • Qwen AI: Used for generating visual assets and images for the game's interface and lunar environment.
  • Claude: Assisted in improving, organizing, and refining the project's technical documentation.
  • Perplexity AI: Supported scientific research by locating NASA publications, technical reports, and information about lunar exploration.
  • Pixabay: Provided music and sound effects to enhance the game's audiovisual experience.

AI tools supported the development process, while the project's concept, gameplay direction, and final decisions were guided by the team.
